If leaks are observed, raise corrective maintenance notification. g) Check valve stem clamp and turn buckle are tight and feedback arm is secure. Perform cleaning activities (rust removal), retighten and adjust wherever necessary. h) Check that the hand-wheel coupling is set to neutral position (wherever applicable). B. VALVE BODY a) Check packing box for sign of leakage. If leak is detected, tighten the packing gland. If leak continues, raise corrective maintenance notification. b) Check valve stem for sign of side loading. If the side loading is noticed, check packing gland position. Perform cleaning activities (rust removal), tighten loose parts, lubricate moving parts and replace damaged parts wherever necessary. b) Inspect all cables for damage and ensure proper mounting integrity. Perform insulation repair and replace damaged cable ties wherever necessary. c) Check that all cable glands are properly installed and seals are in good condition. Perform cleaning activities and replace damaged parts wherever necessary.

normalized_text: PM,6M-EESIFLO EASZ-2 ANALYZER MAINTENANC PM,6M-EESIFLO EASZ-2 ANALYZER MAINTENANCE **************************************************************** Physical Inspection 1. Check for any signs of damage to the cables, glands, body, the glass viewing window or leaking petroleum products. Two-Point Calibration This is the recommend form of on-site calibration to ensure that your units are set to a higher accuracy. If this calibration is performed correctly the accuracy of the readings is ± 0.1% 1. Ensure that the pipeline is in operation and flowing full of clean oil of the type and grade required without any air bubbles or foreign particles 2. Connect a computer to the EASZ-2 with an original USB-RS or USB-CL Com Cable. 3. Start the EASZ-2 software and click the “Measuring” tab 4. Take a sample of the oil from the sampling point just in front of the EASZ-2 unit. This needs to be sent to the lab for testing to determine the real water content (%). 5. For each sample of oil taken from the pipeline record the actual ADC and Temperature values displayed at the top of the “Measuring” tab. 6. Enter the values into a table and repeat the process for a wide range of water contents in the oil. 7. After the results of the samples are sent back from the lab fill in the rest of the table and determine the maximum and minimum % values. 8. Before setting the low and high points in the software ensure that there is at least a 10 value difference between the maximum and minimum values. 9. Connect a computer to the EASZ-2 using an original USB-RS or USB-CL Com Cable. 10. Start the EASZ-2 software, click the “Calibration” tab and select the Two-Point Calibration option. 11. Add the min ADC and Temp values from the table and the actual % Water Content value from the lab to the low-point fields and then press the “Set Low-Point” button. 12. Add the max ADC and Temp values from the table and the actual % Water Content value from the lab to the high-point fields and then press the “Set High-Point” button.
scope: Physical inspection, oil sampling, laboratory water-content testing, ADC and temperature recording, low-point calibration, high-point calibration

normalized_text: PM,6M-RKI M2A OXYGEN ANALYZER MAINTENANC PM,6M-RKI M2A OXYGEN ANALYZER MAINTENANCE **************************************************************** Response Time Determination 1. Place the M2A into its calibration mode or disable external alarms. 2. Note the current gas reading displayed at the M2A 3. Screw the regulator into the 100% nitrogen calibration cylinder 4. Use the flexible tubing coming from the calibration adapter/splash guard to connect the regulator to the calibration adapter/splash guard 5. Turn the regulator’s on/off knob counterclockwise to open the regulator. Gas will begin to flow. Take note of the time or start a stopwatch 6. When you first start to notice a decrease in the gas reading, note how much time passed between starting the gas flow and noticing a reading response 7. Turn the regulator’s on/off knob clockwise to close the regulator. 8. Unscrew the regulator from the calibration cylinder. 9. Disconnect the calibration adapter/splash guard’s flexible tubing from the regulator. NOTE: Do not disconnect the flexible tubing from the calibration adapter/splash guard 10. Add 1 minute to the length of time determined in step 6. This is the response time for the detector. When performing a fresh air adjustment or zero adjustment, gas must be applied for this length of time Analyzer Calibration (Adjust fresh air reading) 1. While in normal operation, press and hold the UP/YES button for 5 seconds to enter Calibration Mode. Release the button when the "Calib?" screen appears 2. If you want to continue with calibration, press and release the UP/YES button to continue. The display will indicate OXYGEN CAL Mode for a few seconds before showing FreshAir Adjust? 3. To continue with adjusting the fresh air (span) reading, press and release the UP/YES button. ENTER will alternate with FreshAir on the top display line and the current oxygen reading will be on the bottom display line 4. Screw the zero air cylinder into the fixed flow regulator 5. Use the flexible tubing coming from the calibration adapter/splash guard to connect the regulator to the calibration adapter 6. Turn the regulator knob counterclockwise to open the regulator. 7. Allow zero air to flow for the length of time determined in “Determining Response Time” 8.Turn the regulator knob clockwise to close the regulator 9. Unscrew the zero air cylinder from the fixed flow regulator. Leave the calibration adapter/splash guard’s flexible tubing connected to the regulator. The M2A will continue to display the maximum gas response on the display and retain the response level in its memory. 10. Press and release the ENTER button. The M2A will perform a fresh air adjustment and the display will indicate ZERO w/Cal Gas?. Analyzer Calibration (Adjust zero setting) 1. If you want to continue with adjusting the zero setting, press and release the UP/YES button. APPLY will alternate with ZERO Gas on the top display line and the current gas reading will be on the bottom display line. 2. Screw the 100% nitrogen gas cylinder into the fixed flow regulator 3. Turn the regulator knob counterclockwise to open the regulator 4. Allow calibration gas to flow for the length of time determined in “Determining Response Time” 5. Turn the regulator knob clockwise to close it 6. Unscrew the calibration gas cylinder from the fixed flow regulator. The M2A will continue to display the minimum gas response on the display and retain the response level in its memory. 7. Adjust the oxygen reading up or down to match the 100% nitrogen cylinder oxygen concentration of 0% by using the UP/YES and DOWN/NO buttons 8. The M2A will perform a zero operation. The display will indicate ZERO Gas PASS for a few seconds, then .indicate ZERO Gas SAVED before indicating Leaving CAL Mode for a few seconds 9. The display will now alternate between the normal operation screen and the message REMOVE CAL GAS for 1 minute. If the calibration gas has not been removed from the detector, remove it now to avoid unwanted alarms. During this 1 minute period, the signal output will remain fixed at 17.4 mA and the relays will remain in their non-alarm state to avoid unwanted alarms while the calibration gas clears from the detector. At the end of the 1 minute period, the REMOVE CAL GAS message will stop appearing and the M2A will return to normal operation 10.Disconnect the calibration adapter/splash guard’s flexible tubing from the regulator 11. Store the components of the calibration kit in a safe place
scope: Detector response-time test, fresh-air adjustment, zero adjustment with nitrogen, calibration-gas removal, return to normal operation

Wire Ropes a) Lubricate wire ropes as necessary. b) Examine end fittings on hoist ropes. c) Examine hoist rope connection to swivel on hook. d) Ensure ropes are spooled correctly on drums. e) Check entire length of wire rope main hoist and boom hoist for kinks, strand nicking, birdcage, high strand, fatigue damage or broken wire. If rope is damaged, cut damaged portion if the remaining length is sufficient for operational purposes. i.e. At least three-(3) layers of rope left on the drum with hook lowered down to sea level. If not, replace wire rope. Please note that the maximum wear off in diameter percentage is 10%. Refer to API RP2D, Sections 3.4.2 and 3.4.3. f) For inspection and replacement criteria: Run wire rope up and down to sea level to check proper spooling of rope on the drum g) Test the main hoist limit switch by carefully raising the main hoist until the overhaul ball touches the over-hoist limit weight. Adjust limit as necessary if not operating correctly, clean and remove dirt or rust from over-hoist limit valve plunger, inspect all moving parts and grease external parts with Gadus S1 OGH150 00 grease. If limit switch assembly is found to be defective, repair or replace parts as necessary for inspection replacement criteria. Hydraulic System - with Electric Motor or Engine Running a) Check for leaks around machinery. b) Check hydraulic hoses for leaks and chaffing. c) Trace all hoses and check for crack in external rubber, particularly in areas where hose is sharply bent. d) Operate each crane function separately and check for oil leaks when system is under pressure. e) Check filters dP for clogging. Top up as required with Omala 150 Oil. Ensure that vent plug is not blocked / painted. e) Fully open the winch valve and lock in position. Rotating/Slew Mechanism a) Check security of slew ring bolts (Hammer check). b) Check security of slew pinion, also checking for wear on pinions / slew ring. Apply open gear lubricant to slew ring gear and slew drive pinion gear. antirust penetrates. c) Check operation of slew parking brake. d) Apply approximately one full grease gun of Gadus S2 V220 2 grease to each of the grease nipples fitted to the upper works for lubrication of the slewing bearing. Dynamic a) Position the boom in 2 or 3 positions with a load suspended and measure the hook radius accurately. normalized_text: PS,12M,DELUGE OPERATION INDICATION CHECK PS,12M,DELUGE OPERATION INDICATION CHECK ***************************************************** Control room operators are to be aware of the operation / status of the deluge system. 2.1 Check Deluge Operation Indication Operational status of the deluge system shall be indicated in the control room. This would give an indication in the control room regarding operational status. ASSURANCE MEASURE : 2.1 Deluge operation control room indication is functioning

normalized_text: PS,12M,DELUGE ACTUATION TEST PS,12M,DELUGE ACTUATION TEST ***************************************************** The deluge system is to deliver firewater upon demand. 3.1 Perform Deluge Valve Actuation Test From the receipt of the initiation signal, the deluge valve opens i. Activate the valve from control room. ii. Verify the valve direction indicator ASSURANCE MEASURE : 3.1 Deluge valve operates on demand

normalized_text: PS,12M,DELUGE INITIATION TEST PS,12M,DELUGE INITIATION TEST ***************************************************** The deluge system is to deliver firewater upon demand. 3.2 Perform Deluge Initiation Test Each of the following methods of deluge initiation shall be operable, where applicable. Operation of the manual release valve at the deluge cabinet / set. iii. Manual push button / soft switch in the control room iv. Fusible tubing (where practical) v. Loss of instrument air / gas. ASSURANCE MEASURE : 3.2 Deluge initiates as per specification

Blast / fire walls, including supporting steelwork and welded / bolted connections ii. Pipe penetrations and cable transits in blast / fire walls and decks. iii. normalized_text: PS,48M-SMOKE/GAS MIG. PREV. MAT. INSP. PS,48M-SMOKE/GAS MIG. PREV. MAT. INSP. ***************************************************** To be able to prevent the migration of hazardous gas and smoke between adjacent areas. 3.1 Perform Smoke / Gas Migration Prevention Material Condition Inspection. i. Designated blast / fire walls, bulkheads and decks, including connections, that provide a segregation barrier between adjacent areas shall show no damage or deterioration that introduces a significant communication path ii. Cable transits and pipe penetrations shall be in place and sealing arrangements complete. iii. normalized_text: PS,12M,HELIDECK FOAM EQUIP INSPECTION PS,12M,HELIDECK FOAM EQUIP INSPECTION ***************************************************** To provide an application of foam in sufficient quantity and quality on the helideck / helicopter refuelling skid irrespective of the wind direction. 1.1 Perform Helideck Foam Equipment Inspection The helideck foam system shall meet, but not limited, to the following requirements: i. No visible damage to the equipment. ii. The foam monitor oscillation is to be operable. iii. The foam branch manual shutoff valve is to be operable. iv. The foam eductor allowing adjustment of foam concentration shall be operable. v. The foam monitors and foam branches are capable of effective helideck coverage. vi. The maximum shelf life of foam is within 10 years from date of manufacture and the quality of the concentrate is per specification. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.1a Helideck foam equipment in good condition. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.1b Helideck foam concentrate is within specification and shelf life is not exceeded.
scope: Inspect equipment condition, check monitor oscillation, operate shutoff valves and eductors, verify coverage, check foam quality and shelf life

normalized_text: PS,12M,HELIDECK FOAM EQUIP TEST PS,12M,HELIDECK FOAM EQUIP TEST ***************************************************** To provide an application of foam in sufficient quantity and quality on the helideck / helicopter refuelling skid irrespective of the wind direction. 1.2 Perform Helideck Foam Equipment (In-Service) Test i. The foam production equipment should be activated using water only to confirm the jet range and spray pattern of the system. ii. The helideck foam system shall meet the following requirements: Every monitor shall be capable of being initiated on the helideck from each of the Helicopter Landing Officer (HLO) activation points. All local monitor activation points are to be operable. All foam branch systems are to be operable. Notes: 1. Routine periodic testing of performance in the offshore environment can be achieved by operating the equipment using water (refer to NFPA 11). 2. Foam Production Performance (Acceptance) Test: The helideck foam system shall meet the following requirements when the equipment is newly installed, when significant maintenance, refurbishment or component replacement has been undertaken or recommissioning / recertification of helidecks is being conducted: Every monitor shall be capable of being initiated on the helideck from each of the Helicopter Landing Officer (HLO) activation points. Delivery of foam to the helideck must be achieved in less than 30 seconds from initiation. All local monitor activation points are to be operable. All foam branch systems are to be operable. An effective and complete foam blanket should be produced across the solid floor area. The produced foam (finished foam) concentration to be within specified tolerance. This shall be verified via lab analysis of fire performance testing. There shall be sufficient standby quantity of foam liquid stored close to the skid for a minimum of 10 minutes duration for each of the helideck monitors. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.2 Helideck foam system test acceptable.

normalized_text: PS,12M,FOAM TANK INSPECTION PS,12M,FOAM TANK INSPECTION ***************************************************** To provide an application of foam in sufficient quantity and quality on the helideck / helicopter refuelling skid irrespective of the wind direction. 1.3 Inspect Foam Tank Condition and Contents i. The foam system(s) concentrate tanks are to be filled to the correct level with the correct concentrate not less than the minimum operational stock calculated as per country specific aviation regulation. ii. There shall be sufficient foam supply capacity for a minimum prescribed period of discharge from the system. iii. Foam tank system shall be in good working condition, correctly labelled and free from any mechanical damage. iv. Check foam tank thickness and free from corrosion. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.3b Foam tank system are in good working condition.
scope: Check concentrate type and level, verify supply capacity, inspect condition and labels, check tank thickness and corrosion

normalized_text: PS,12M,ANALYSE FOAM CONCENTRATE PS,12M,ANALYSE FOAM CONCENTRATE ***************************************************** To provide an application of foam in sufficient quantity and quality on the helideck / helicopter refuelling skid irrespective of the wind direction. 1.4 Analyse Foam Concentrate Confirm by testing that the quality of produced foam (concentrated foam) is within the correct specification - refer to National Fire Protection Agency (NFPA 11 - Foam systems). normalized_text: PS,12M,PORTABLE FIRE EXT INSPECTION PS,12M,PORTABLE FIRE EXT INSPECTION ***************************************************** To provide suitable dry powder in sufficient quantity to extinguish aviation fuel fire on the helideck. 2.1 Perform an Inspection of the Portable fire extinguisher to confirm that: i. normalized_text: PS,12M,FWP DETAIL INSPECTION PS,12M,FWP DETAIL INSPECTION ***************************************************** Each firewater pump shall operate in accordance with its design characteristic. 4.1 Perform Detail Inspection of Fire Water Pump The inspection scope to cover: Alignment, Cable/wire insulation, Engine crankcase breather, Exhaust system and drain condensate trap, Flexible hoses and connections, Fuel Tank Vents and Overflow, Plumbing parts in & outside of LCP panels, Shaft movement or endplay while running, and Suction screens Note: 1. If the fire water pump diesel driver is fitted with overspeed protection, the function test is to be conducted with a frequency determined by the site. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 4.1 Physical integrity of the Fire Water Pump System is intact.
scope: Inspect alignment, insulation, breather, exhaust and drain trap, hoses, connections, vents, plumbing, shaft movement, suction screens, caisson and anodes

normalized_text: PS,12M,FWP MAINTENANCE PS,12M,FWP MAINTENANCE ***************************************************** Each firewater pump shall operate in accordance with its design characteristic. 4.3 Perform Fire Water Pump maintenance Carry out maintenance on the following but not limited: i. Batteries ii. Circulating water filter iii. Control and power wiring connections iv. Electrical connections v. Controller per manufacturer requirements vi. Diesel engine system per manufacturer requirements vii. Electric motor and power system per manufacturer requirements viii. Engine oil & Filter annually or 50 operating hours (whichever comes first). ix. Fuel tank check for water and foreign materials x. Measure back pressure on engine turbo xi. Pressure gauges and sensors xii. Pump / motor bearings and coupling or as Required xiii. Sacrificial anode Note: 1.Refer to Fire Water Pump Annual Maintenance checklist for detailed test activities 2.OEM recommendation shall be considered when determining frequency of maintenance. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 4.3 Fire Water Pump maintenance is conducted with no anomalies reported
scope: Maintain batteries, filters, wiring, controllers, drivers, oil and filter, fuel tank, gauges, sensors, bearings, couplings, anodes

normalized_text: PS,12M,FWP PERFORMANCE TEST PS,12M,FWP PERFORMANCE TEST ***************************************************** Each firewater pump shall operate in accordance with its design characteristic. 4.2 Perform Fire Water Pump Performance (Flow) Test An annual test of each pump assembly shall be conducted by qualified personnel under no-flow (churn), rated flow at 100% and 150% of the pump rated flow capacity of the fire pump by controlling the quantity of water discharged through approved test devices. The following shall be performed on top of the above: i. Diesel fuel testing ii. Fire pump alarm signals iii. Main relief valve iv. Power transfer switch v. Supervisory signal for high cooling water temperature Note: 1. If available suction supplies do not allow flowing of 150% of the rated pump capacity, the fire pump shall be permitted to operate at maximum allowable discharge. 2. Refer to Fire Water Pump Annual Test checklist for detailed test activities 3. For floating facilities, the requirement for performance test shall require firewater pump testing for 100% of rated flow and rated discharge pressure ASSURANCE MEASURE: 4.2a Fire Water Pump pressure rate is as per design ASSURANCE MEASURE: 4.2b Fire Water Pump flow rate is as per design
scope: Test churn flow, rated flow and maximum flow, test diesel fuel, alarms, relief valve, transfer switch, cooling-water supervisory signal

normalized_text: PS,60M,FW CAISSON INTERNAL INSP & MAINT PS,60M,FW CAISSON INTERNAL INSP & MAINT ***************************************************** Each firewater pump shall operate in accordance with its design characteristic. 4.4 Perform Fire Water Caisson/Tank Internal Inspection and Maintenance. i. Caisson internal inspection via underwater camera. ii. Caisson internal cleaning/ debris retrieval (if any anomaly found from camera inspection) Note: 1. normalized_text: PS,1M,FWP VISUAL INSPECTION PS,1M,FWP VISUAL INSPECTION ***************************************************** To ensure the fire water pump is in good operating condition and free from any physical damage 1.1 Perform Visual Inspection on Fire Water Pump System This should include but not limited to: i. Pumps, Motors, Engines, Controllers, Batteries, Fuel Systems, Switches, Gauges, Fire Water Caissons/Tank ii. Lubricants, Coolant, Piping, Isolation Valves, Relief Valves and Pump House as applicable, and Jockey Pump (if provided) power supply Note: 1. Refer to the facility s Fire Water Pump Weekly Inspection checklist for complete activity list ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.1 Physical integrity of the Fire Water Pump System intact.

normalized_text: PS,1M,DIESEL ENGINE FWP FLOW TEST PS,1M,DIESEL ENGINE FWP FLOW TEST ***************************************************** Fire Water Pump shall start on demand from initiation signals. Each pump shall be capable of running without interruption for the duration of a defined emergency event. 2.1 Perform Fire Water Pump Flow Test Diesel engine-driven fire pump i. to test run the pump and observe water flow ii. test pump operation philosophy (pressure drop) - if any Note: 1. Refer to Fire Water Pump Weekly Flow Test checklist for checks to be made while engine is running. 2. This is an SOP task and not listed in PMMS. 3. Start each pump by using one of the installed starting devices each time; this should be carried out on a weekly rotating basis. ASSURANCE MEASURE : 2.1 Pump driver starts appropriately and runs for 30 minutes
scope: Start and run pump, observe water flow, test pressure-drop operation, verify 30-minute uninterrupted operation

normalized_text: PS,3M,FWP ITPM PS,3M,FWP ITPM ***************************************************** Fire Water Pump shall start on demand from initiation signals. 3.1 Perform ITPM on Fire Water Pump System This is to include but not limited to the following: i. Engine crankcase breather ii. Battery terminals cleaned and tightened iii. Cooling line water strainers and fuel strainer/ filter iv. Battery state of charging and charge rate v. Insulation and fire hazards check/ inspection vi. Fire main pressure switch vii. Fire detection on F&G panel viii. Local panel push button ix. F&G push button Note: Refer to Fire Water Pump Quarterly ITPM checklist for complete activity list. ASSURANCE MEASURE : 3.1 Fire Water Pump System is in good working condition.
scope: Inspect crankcase breather, clean and tighten battery terminals, inspect strainers and filters, check battery charging, inspect insulation and fire hazards, test pressure switch and initiation controls

normalized_text: PS,12M,FW RING MAIN HEADER VISUAL INSP PS,12M,FW RING MAIN HEADER VISUAL INSP ***************************************************** The firewater ring main is to distribute firewater at the required pressures and flow rates for the end users. 1.1 Perform Firewater Ring Main Header Visual Inspection i. There should be no leaks. ii. Pipe supports are in place and secure. iii. There shall be no significant visible deterioration of firewater ring main header pipework. Note: Ref: API RP 14G and API RP14E -Section 5. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.1a No unacceptable deterioration on ring main ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.1b No unacceptable leaks on ring main
scope: Check for leaks, verify pipe supports, inspect pipework deterioration

normalized_text: PS,12M,FIREWATER RING MAIN PRESS CHECK PS,12M,FIREWATER RING MAIN PRESS CHECK ***************************************************** The firewater ring main pressure is to be maintained at the specified level. 2.1 Confirm Firewater Ring Main Pressure is Maintained at a Specified Pressure Duty or Standby fire water pumps shall start at set falling ring main header pressure to maintain ring main header at set pressure. i. check pressure read from pressure gauge Note: 1. Refer to API RP 14G and API RP14E - Section 5. 2. Maintained pressure should be recorded at most remote location from fire water pump. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 2.1 Ring main maintained at correct pressure
scope: Check pressure gauge, confirm pump start at falling pressure, record pressure at remote location

normalized_text: PS,12M,MONITOR FUNCTION TEST PS,12M,MONITOR FUNCTION TEST ***************************************************** To supply fixed appliances for manual firefighting. 4.1 Perform Monitor Function Test The fire monitors shall be capable of the following functions: i. The monitors are operable ii. Can manually actuate iii. Oscillate (where applicable) iv. Locking devices are in place v. Monitors including adjustment of the nozzle (if fitted) are operable. Note: Refer to API RP 14G and API RP14E - Section 5. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 4.1 Fire Monitors are in an acceptable condition
scope: Check operation, manual actuation, oscillation, locking devices, nozzle adjustment

normalized_text: PS,12M,ISOLATION VALVE INSPECTION PS,12M,ISOLATION VALVE INSPECTION ***************************************************** To enable isolation of damaged sections of the ring main whilst providing firewater. 5.1 Perform Isolation Valve Inspection i. Confirm that all isolation valves permit isolation of ring main sections, hydrants and monitors. ii. Confirm that all isolation valves are either normally open or locked open as required with easily removable means (e.g. tie-wrap). Note: Refer to API RP 14G and API RP14E - Section 5. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 5.1a Isolation valves are fitted. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 5.1b Isolation valves are locked openas required
scope: Verify isolation capability, confirm normal-open position, check locking-open arrangements

normalized_text: PS,48M-PSSIVE FIRE PROTECTION INSPECTION PS,48M-PSSIVE FIRE PROTECTION INSPECTION ***************************************************** To maintain the integrity of the structure, plant and safety systems in the event of a fire using cementitious or resin based PFP. 1.1 Perform Passive Fire Protection Inspection of Structures Demonstrate that there is no significant visible damage, or deterioration, in the PFP system. There shall be: i. No visible open vertical cracks. ii. No disbonding of the resin-based PFP leading to the exposure of the steel substrate. iii. No attachments to a PFP coated structural element with no or insufficient remedial coatback. iv. No accumulation of water under coating / PFP coating. v. No modification on structure / equipment with PFP not reinstated or properly repaired. vi. Brickwork fireproofing is without cracks and loose joints. NOTE: 1. Visible surface cracks to the top coat, or mechanical impact which penetrates the top coat, should be recorded during the inspection but does not constitute a FAIL. 2. Any anomaly shall be referred to Technical Authority. 3. PFP shall include Cryogenic protection where applicable. 4. This task is conducted under SI002 and SI009. Coating condition to be inspected by MCI. ASSURRANCE MEASURE: 1.1 PFP of Structure within specification.
scope: Inspect cracks, disbonding, exposed steel, attachments and coatback, trapped water, unreinstated modifications, brickwork joints, coating condition

normalized_text: PS,3M,FINE WATER SPRAY SYS VISUAL INSP PS,3M,FINE WATER SPRAY SYS VISUAL INSP ***************************************************** To provide a water mist to extinguish fires. 1.1 Perform Fine Water Spray Mist System Visual Inspection. The Fine Water Spray System shall meet the following criteria upon visual inspection: i. Protected enclosures are secure and intact. ii. Water reservoirs / cylinders are full. iii. The compressed air / nitrogen cylinders associated with the fine water spray system shall be charged to levels required by the OEM iv. System cabinets are free of water ingress ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.1 Fine Water Spray is in an acceptable condition
scope: Inspect protected enclosures, check reservoir and cylinder levels, check air or nitrogen charge, inspect cabinets for water ingress

normalized_text: PS,12M,FINE WATER SPRAY MANUAL INITIATE PS,12M,FINE WATER SPRAY MANUAL INITIATE ***************************************************** To provide a water mist to extinguish fires. 1.2 Verify Fine Water Spray System Manual Initiation Manual initiation of the Fine Water Spray System is to be operable from all defined locations, as applicable: i. Local (on the system). ii. Outside the module (outside protected enclosure). iii. Control room. Note: Initiation to be done without the need to discharge medium. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.2 Fine Water Spray operates on demand.
scope: Test manual initiation locally, outside protected enclosure, from control room, verify operation without medium discharge

normalized_text: PS,12M,FINE WATER SPRAY SYS FUNC TEST PS,12M,FINE WATER SPRAY SYS FUNC TEST ***************************************************** To provide a water mist to extinguish fires. 1.3 Fine Water Spray System Function Test The Fine Water Spray System shall perform the following functions upon initiation: i. Initiation delay of the Fine Water Spray System shall be a minimum of xx seconds (to allow for HVAC shutdown and damper closure). ii. Enclosure / Room Dampers close. iii. Local fuel supply isolates. iv. System nozzles are clear. v. Function test is as per the F&G Cause and Effect Matrix. Note: Confirmation that the nozzles are clear can be by system wet discharge or delivery of air through the discharge pipework and nozzles. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.3a Fine Water Spray acceptable functional test. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.3b Initiation delay time as per design (xx seconds)
scope: Verify initiation delay, damper closure, fuel isolation, clear nozzles, test Fire and Gas cause-and-effect functions

normalized_text: PS,12M,FINE WATER SPRAY AUTO INITIATE PS,12M,FINE WATER SPRAY AUTO INITIATE ***************************************************** Fine Water Spray Extinguishing systems shall be automatically initiated in accordance with the Fire & Gas Detection Philosophy/ Cause & Effects. 2.1 Automatic Initiation Perform a functional test to confirm activation of the Fine Water Spray system in accordance with the FGS Cause & Effect. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 2.1Fine Water Spray system acceptable activation test

normalized_text: PS,48M,PROTECTIVE RELAY PS,48M,PROTECTIVE RELAY ***************************************************** To protect the electrical system against failures. 1.1 Perform electrical protective relays calibration. Calibration includes the following: i. Setting as per protection report ii. Visual check for mechanical integrity iii. Function testing at relay setting iv. Function tripping circuit v. Check CT winding continuity ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.1 Electrical protective relays operating within its specification.
scope: Verify protection settings, inspect mechanical integrity, function-test relay settings, test tripping circuit, check current-transformer winding continuity

normalized_text: PS,12M,FOAM EQUIP INSPECTION PS,12M,FOAM EQUIP INSPECTION ***************************************************** To provide foam in sufficient quantity and quality to extinguish or limit the spread of process / tank fire. 1.1 Perform Foam Equipment Inspection The foam system shall meet the following requirements: i. No visible damage to the equipment. ii. The foam monitor oscillation is to be operable. iii. The foam branch manual shutoff valve is to be operable. iv. The foam monitors and foam branches are capable of effective process area coverage. v. The maximum shelf life of foam is 10 years and the quality of the concentrate must meet performance requirements (physical properties and fire performance). Note: 1. Criteria can be demonstrated via the use of water as opposed to foam. 2. Foam systems need to be tested in two ways, firstly by ensuring the system is in working order and secondly by analysing samples of foam concentrate and finished foam. 3. The discharge of significant quantities of finished foam to the sea has potential to pollute the environment. Therefore, the methodology for testing foam and equipment performance should be carried out with a view to minimising the potential for pollution to occur. In addition, any use of fluorine-based foam shall undergo additional requirements per Petronas Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) requirements. 4. Systems should be tested, and quality assured before installation to ensure that foam (particularly 1% inducted) meets its performance parameters. This would normally be done onshore, with the finished foam contained and suitably treated. 5. Routine periodic testing of performance in the offshore environment should be achieved by operating the equipment initially using water only and subsequently confirming by production of a limited amount of finished foam captured for testing. Testing of this finished foam and a sample of the foam concentrate should be conducted by an accredited foam test house against the applicable laboratory standard (e.g. BS5306, NFPA11 etc.) ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.1 Foam equipment is functional and in good condition.
scope: Inspect equipment damage, test monitor oscillation, test branch shutoff valves, verify area coverage, check foam shelf life and quality, sample foam concentrate and finished foam

normalized_text: PS,12M,FOAM SYS TEST PS,12M,FOAM SYS TEST ***************************************************** To provide foam in sufficient quantity and quality to extinguish or limit the spread of process / tank fire. 1.2 Perform Foam System Test The foam system shall meet the following requirements: i. Every monitor shall be capable of being initiated locally. ii. Delivery of foam to the process area must be achieved in less than 30 seconds from initiation. iii. All local monitor activation points are to be operable. iv. All foam branch systems are to be operable. v. An effective and complete foam blanket should be produced across the solid floor area. vi. The foam liquid is normally a 3% AFFF solution with specified tolerance of +/-10%. vii. There shall be a sufficient quantity of foam liquid stored in each unit for a minimum specified duration for each of the monitors. viii. Where applicable, foam concentrate pumps and foam proportioners are able to deliver the required foam concentrate flow and pressure. Notes: 1. A test of 10 minutes duration is not necessary to demonstrate the above criteria. Sufficient foam system capacity / application duration is demonstrated by a combination of the foam tanks being filled to the correct level AND the produced foam being the correct concentration. 2. The performance standard is not met if any of the above criteria are not satisfied. 3. Other foam system designs may incorporate different type of equipment (e.g. high back pressure foam generators, around the pump foam proportioner, compressed air foam system). Refer NFPA 11 for SSPS development as these may differ in its performance standards. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.2 Foam system is able to function as required.
scope: Test local monitor initiation, verify foam delivery time, test activation points and branches, verify foam blanket, concentration and stored quantity, check pump and proportioner flow and pressure

normalized_text: PS,12M,FOAM TANK INSPECTION PS,12M,FOAM TANK INSPECTION ***************************************************** To provide foam in sufficient quantity and quality to extinguish or limit the spread of process / tank fire. 1.3 Inspect Foam Tank Condition and Contents i. The foam system(s) concentrate tanks are to be filled to the correct level with the correct concentrate. There shall be a sufficient foam supply capacity for a minimum prescribed period of discharge from the system. ii. Foam tank system shall be in good working condition, correctly labelled and free from any mechanical damage. iii. Foam tank is protected from direct sunlight. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.3a Foam tank contents within specification. ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.3b Foam tank system are in good working condition.
scope: Check fill level and concentrate type, verify supply capacity, inspect condition and labeling, check mechanical damage and sunlight protection

normalized_text: PS,12M,ANALYSE FOAM CONCENTRATE PS,12M,ANALYSE FOAM CONCENTRATE ***************************************************** To provide foam in sufficient quantity and quality to extinguish or limit the spread of process / tank fire. 1.4 Analyse Foam Concentrate Confirm by testing that the quality of produced foam (finished foam) is within the correct specification - refer to National Fire Protection Agency (NFPA 11 - Foam systems). Note: The tolerance of the foam specifications will depend on the foam type (AFFF, AR, FFFP etc.). ASSURANCE MEASURE: 1.4 Produced foam within specification.

normalized_text: PS,1M,DESANDER OPERATING PS,1M,DESANDER OPERATING ***************************************************** To remove solids (sand) from the process stream. 1.1 Ensure the Desander is working under operating envelope. Monitor the following parameters as part of regular monitoring and performance efficiency check of the unit. i. Pressure drop across the system: Inlet Pressure & Outlet Pressure ii. Sand count / Particle Size Distribution (PSD) analysis: At Inlet & outlet of desander. iii. Total liquid and gas flow rate (i.e. by well test) passing through the system. iv. Desander / Sand Filtration Clean out (where applicable): Frequency to be determined by rate of sand production/ accumulation, and carryout critical maintenance activity in line with OEM recommendations. STROKE THE VALVE USING THE CONTROLLER OUTPUT, i.e,50% AND SPECIFIED RANGE.CHECK THE EQUIVALENT INDICATOR SCALE ON THE VALVE.RECTIFY ANY DISCREPANCY. vii) ENSURE THAT THE "VENT" ON THE BACK OF THE POSITIONER CASE IS OPEN AND CLEAR. viii) CHECK COVER GASKET FOR DAMAGE AND SECURE COVER k) WHILST CARRYING OUT CHECKS, CHECK OPERATION OF LIMIT SWITCHES,IF ANY , i) LUBRICATE THE LEVER MECHANISM OF VALVE POSITION / LIMIT SWITCH WITH SILICON BASED LUBRICANTS SUCH AS DOW CORNING NO.33 OR EQUIVALENT . ii) ENSURE THAT THE SWITCH HOUSING IS FREE FROM MOISTURE CONDENSATION . iii) ENSURE THAT THE LEVER MECHANISM MOVES FREELY WITHOUT RUBBING AGAINST STATIONARY PARTS. iv) TIGHTEN LOCKSCREWS. v) ENSURE THAT THE VALVE POSITION / LIMIT SWITCH TRAVEL IS SMOOTH. vi) PERFORM FUNCTIONAL LOOP TESTING TO VERIFY THE RELEVANT LOOP RESPONSES AND COLLECT EFFECT OF ALARM(ASD) ACTIVATED ACCORDINGLY. vii) ENSURE THAT THE VALVE POSITION INDICATION CORRESPONCE WITH THE ACTUAL VALVE POSITION STATUS. 3. VALVE BODY a) INSPECT VALVE BODY AND STEM FOR CORROSION AND DAMAGE. b) CHECK FLANGE, BONNET BOLTS AND DRAIN PLUG FOR TIGHTNESS. c) CHECK FOR LEAKAGE AROUND VALVE STEM AND TIGHTEN PACKING FLANGE NUTS AS NECESSARY. d) BEFORE TAKING THE VALVE OUT OF SERVICE. IF PRACTICAL LISTEN FOR VALVE SEAT LEAKAGE WHEN VALVE IS FULLY CLOSED. (IF VALVE SEAT LEAKAGE CAN BE HEARD REPORT TO SUPERVISOR). NOTE : i) REPLACE ALL DEFECTIVE PARTS. ii) LET THE SUPERVISOR KNOW OF ANY ABNORMAL FINDINGS. iii) FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION CONSULT THE PRODUCT TECHNICAL MANUAL. iv) RECORD ANY ERRORS / FAULTS IN THE MAINTENANCE SYSTEM. PRESSURE TRANSMITTER ( ELECTRONIC ) IPT04E 1. THE INSTRUMENT MUST BE ISOLATED FROM THE THE PROCESS LINE AND DEPRESSURISED BEFORE WORKING ON THE UNIT UNLESS THE UNIT IS IN SAFE AREA . * TEST TERMINALS 2. THE TEST TERMINALS ARE AVAILABLE FOR IN-PROCESS CHECKS. THE TERMINALS ARE CONNECTED ACROSS A DIODE THROUGH WHICH THE LOOP SIGNAL CURRENT PASSES . THE INDICATING METER OR TEST EQUIPMENT SHUNTS THE DIODE WHEN CONNECTED TO THE TEST TERMINALS IS KEEP BELOW THE DIODE'S THRESHOLD VOLTAGE,NO CURRENT PASSES THROUGH THE DIODE.TO ASSURE THAT THERE IS NO LEAKAGE CURRENT THROUGH THE DIODE WHEN A TEST READING IS BEING MADE OR WHEN AN INDICATING METER IS CONNECTED, THE RESISTANCE OF THE TEST CONNECTION OR METER SHOULD NOT EXCEED 10 OHMS FOR 4-20mA DC MODEL . * SENSING ELEMENT CHECK OUT 3. THE SENSING ELEMENT IS NOT FIELD REPAIRABLE AND MUST BE REPLACED IF FOUND TO BE DEFECTIVE. * CIRCUIT BOARD CHECK OUT 4. THE PRINTED CIRCUIT BOARDS CAN MOST EASILY BE CHECKED FOR MALFUNCTION BY SUBSTITUTING A SPARE INTO THE CIRCUIT. * ELECTRICAL HOUSING 5. EXAMINE CIRCUIT BOARDS TO SEE THAT THEY ARE CLEAN. 6. CHECK THAT "O" RINGS AND SNAP RINGS ARE SECURE ON THE"ZERO" AND "SPAN" ADJUSTMENT SCREWS. 7. ENSURE THAT THE BAYONET CONNECTORS ON THE CONNECTION BOARD ARE CLEAN. 8. ALIGN THE ZERO AND SPAN ADJUSTMENT SCREWS WITH THE POTENTIOMETER THE CALIBRATION BOARDS AND PUSH THE CALIBRATION BOARD ONTO THE BAYONET CONNECTORS. SECURE THE CALIBRATION BOARD WITH THE THREE STANDOFFS.THE UPPER RIGHT-HAND STANDOFF GROUNDS THE ELECTRONICS TO THE CASE AND MUST BE FIRMLY IN PLACE. 9. SLIDE THE HEADER ASSEMBLY BOARD ONTO THE PINS WITH THE COMPONENT SIDE TOWARD THE PINS. SLIDE EXCESS WIRE BEHIND CALIBRATION BOARD. 10. PUSH THE AMPLIFIER BOARD ONTO THE BAYONET CONNECTORS AND SECURE WITH THE HOLDING SCREWS. 11. IF THE TRANSMITTER IS NOT FUNCTIONING PROPERLY AND ABNORMALITIES FOUND ON ITEM 1 UNTIL ITEM 10,THE TRANSMITTER SHALL BE REMOVED FROM THE PROCESS AND CALIBRATE AS FOLLOWS. NOTE : IF THE UNIT IS CONNECTED TO AN ALARM SYSTEM IN THE DCS ENSURE THAT THE ALARM HAS BEEN OVER-RIDDEN . 1.1 CALIBRATION ( WITHOUT ELEVATION OR SUPPRESSION ) a) TEST EQUIPMENT REQUIRED i) CERTIFIED PROCESS CALIBRATOR ii) COMPRESSED AIR iii) POWER SUPPLY(24vDC) iv) DIGITAL MULTIMETER v) HAND PUMP b) CHECK FOR CORROSION AND SECURITY OFINTERNAL CONNECTIONS. c) CHECK THE SPECIFIED TRANSMITTER RANGE AGAINST THE INSTRUMENT SPECIFICATION , DATA SHEET OR TRANSMITTER NAMEPLATE. d) CONNECT UNIT TO A 24vDC POWER SUPPLY AND A CERTIFIED CALIBRATOR TO THE "H" SIDE OF THE UNIT. e) CHECK ZERO. CONFIRM THAT THE OUTPUT TO BE 4mA ACROSS A 100 OHMS RESISTOR IN THE 24vDC SUPPLY TO THE UNIT. OTHERWISE ADJUST THE ZERO ADJUSTMENT SCREW. f) APPLY PRESSURE OF 100% OF THE RANGE AND CONFIRM THAT OUTPUT SIGNAL IS 20mA.OTHERWISE ADJUST THE SPAN ADJUSTMENT SCREW. g) REPEAT STEPS "e" AND "f" UNTIL 4-20mA IS ACHIEVED OVER THE REQUIRED PRESSURE RANGE. h) APPLY PRESSURE OF 50% OF THE RANGE AND ADJUST THE LINEARITY ADJUSTMENT AS NECESSARY UNTIL THE OUTPUT INDICATES 12mA (IF APPLICABLE) i) CARRY OUT APPLY 5 POINTS OF CALIBRATION CHECK AT 0% , 25% , 50% , 75% , AND 100% OF RANGE(RISING & FALLING). THE OUTPUT SHOULD BE 4mA ,8mA,12mA,16mA AND 20mA , RESPECTIVELY . j) IF THE ERROR VARIES OVER +/- 0.25% OF THE SPECIFIED RANGE , MAKE NECESSARY ADJUSTMENTS. k) UPON COMPLETION , TAG ITEM WITH CALIBRATION STICKER . 1.2. CALIBRATION (WITH ELEVATION OR SUPPRESSION) a) APPLY POSITIVE OR NEGATIVE PRESSURE EQUAL TO THE LOW END OF THE REQUIRED SPAN. b) ADJUST THE ZERO TO GIVE AN OUTPUT OF 4mA. c) APPLY PRESSURE TO THE REQUIRED FULL SPAN AND ADJUST SPAN TO GIVE OUTPUT OF 20mA. e) RE-CHECK ZERO. NOTE : THE UNIT MAY HAVE A "SPAN RANGE" SELECTION SWITCH,CHECK THE SELECTION SWITCH SET TO SUIT THE REQUIRED RANGE. f) CHECK CALIBRATION AS PER ITEMS 1.1e TO 1.1j. g) UPON COMPLETION ,TAG ITEM WITH CALIBRATION STICKER . 12. RE-INSTALL THE UNIT INTO PROCESS LINE AND RECONNECT ELECTRICAL WIRING. 13. APPLY PROCESS PRESSURE SLOWLY AND INSPECT FOR LEAKS. 14. CHECK REMOTE PRESSURE INDICSTOR(IF AVAILABLE) SHOWING PRESSURE WITHIN THE CORRECT TRANSMITTER RANGE. 15. ENSURE THAT THE COMPLETE LOOP IS RE-INSTATED TO NORMAL OPERATION UPON JOB COMPLETION. DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE TRANSMITTER (ELECTRONIC) IPT03E THE INSTRUMENT MUST BE ISOLATED FROM THE PROCESS LINE AND DEPRESSURISED BEFORE WORKING ON THE UNIT UNLESS THE UNIT IS IN SAFE AREA . NOTE : IF THE UNIT IS CONNECTED TO AN ALARM SYSTEM IN THE DCS ENSURE THAT THE ALARM HAS BEEN OVER-RIDDEN . 1. CALIBRATION a) TEST EQUIPMENT REQUIRED i) HAND PUMP / HYDRAULIC PUMP / DEAD WEIGHT TESTER ii) COMPRESSED AIR iii) PNEUMATIC CALIBRATOR iv) DC POWER SUPPLY v) DIGITAL MULTIMETER b) CHECK THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE FOR ANY PHYSICAL DAMAGE. c) CHECK THE RANGE AGAINST NAME PLATE OR INSTRUMENT SPECIFICATION. d) PREPARE CALIBRATION TEST SET-UP FOR ELECTRONIC DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE TRANSMITTER. e) OPEN LOW AND HIGH PRESSURE INLET TO ATMOSPHERE.CONFIRM THAT OUTPUT SIGNAL IS 4mA. OTHERWISE, ADJUST THE ZERO SCREW. f) OPEN LOW PRESSURE INLET TO ATMOSPHERE AND APPLY PRESSURE AT 100% OF THE RANGE TO HIGH PRESSURE INLET.CONFIRM THAT OUTPUT SIGNAL IS 20mA. OTHERWISE ADJUST THE SPAN SCREW. g) REPEAT e AND f, AS NECESSARY UNTIL BOTH ZERO AND SPAN ARE WITHIN 0.1mA. h) CARRY OUT 5 POINTS CALIBRATION CHECK AT 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% RANGE(RISING & FALLING).THE OUTPUT SHOULD BE 4mA, 8mA, 12mA AND 20mA , RESPECTIVELY. NOTES : i) CONSIDER ZERO AND RANGE ADJUSTMENT WITH ELEVATION OR SUPPRESSION ATTACHMENT IF IT IS THE CASE. ii) FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION CONSULT THE PRODUCT TECHNICAL MANUAL. iii) LET THE SUPERVISOR KNOW OF ANY ABNORMAL FINDINGS. i) IF READING ERROR AT ANY POINT EXCEEDS 1% OF THE RANGE, MAKE NECESSARY ADJUSTMENTS. j) RECORD ALL THE READINGS IN THE INSTR. CALIBRATION SHEET. k) UPON COMPLETION , TAG ITEM WITH A CALIBRATION STICKER. l) ENSURE THAT THE COMPLETE LOOP IS RE-INSTATED TO NORMAL OPERATION UPON JOB COMPLETION. PNEUMATIC SWITCHING RELAY ISDR1E 1. ISOLATE THE AIR/GAS SUPPLY TO THE RELAY AND DEPRESSURISE THE UNIT. 2. DISASSEMBLE THE RELAY AND CLEAN ALL PARTS. 3. EXAMINE ALL PARTS FOR WEAR, DAMAGE AND CORROSION. 4. IF INDICATORS ARE FITTED, ENSURE THEY ARE CLEAN. 5. CAREFULLY CHECK CONDITION OF "O" RINGS AND IF NECESSARY FIT NEW RING. 6. RE-ASSEMBLE UNIT, ENSURING TO LUBRICATE ALL MOVING PARTS AND "O-RINGS" WITH SILICON BASED LUBRICANTS SUCH AS DOW CORNING NO.33 GREASE OR EQUIVALENT. 7. USING A HAND PUMP CHECK THAT THE RELAY WILL OPERATE CORRECTLY AND IF INDICATORS ARE FITTED, THESE INDICATE THE CORRECT POSITION OF THE RELAY. 8. AFTER RECONNECTION TO THE AIR/GAS SUPPLY, THE SIGNAL AND OUTPUT LINES PRESSURISES THE UNIT AND CHECK FOR LEAKAGE. PNEUMATIC INDICATOR CONTROLLER IPC01E 1. CONTROLLER CALIBRATION a) CONNECT A TEMPORARY PRESSURE REGULATOR TO THE CONTROL CONTROL VALVE KEEP IT OPEN IN A POSITION ACCEPTABLE TO OPERATION. b) SWITCH THE CONTROLLER TO "MANUAL". c) RECORD AS FOUND SETTINGS, i.e. PROPORTIONAL BAND, RESET, DERIVATIVE TIME AND SET POINT INDEX. d) DIS-CONNECT MEASURING ELEMENTS PRESSURE CONNECTIONS AND CONNECT PNEUMATIC CALIBRATOR TEST EQUIPMENT. e) SIMULATE PRESSURE TO MINIMUM RANGE. REFER TO MEASURING ELEMENT NAMEPLATE FOR THE CONTROLLER RANGE. f) ADJUST ZERO SCREW TO BRING THE POINTER TO ZERO. g) SIMULATE PRESSURE TO 100% RANGE. REFER TO MEASURING ELEMENT NAMEPLATE FOR THE CONTROLLER RANGE. h) IF THE CONTROLLER READING IS INCORRECT, USE RANGE SCREW TO POSITION THE POINTER ABOUT HALFWAY TOWARDS THE CORRECT READING i.e., FOR 10% ERROR, ADJUST RANGE 5% TOWARDS CORRECT READING. i) REPEAT ITEM "e"THROUGH "h"UNTIL BOTH READINGS ARE CORRECT. j) DIS-CONNECT THE TEST EQUIPMENT AND RE-CONNECT THE MEASURING ELEMENT PRESSURE CONNECTION. k) CHECK THAT THE PROPORTIONAL BAND, RESET, DERIVATIVE SETTINGS AS RECORDED IN ITEM "c". l) MOVE THE SET POINT INDEX AROUND THE MEASURED VALUE POINTER, ENSURE THE "OUTPUT" RISES & FALLS ACCORDING TO THE CONTROLLER ACTION ,i.e., DIRECT OR REVERSE ACTION. n) MOVE THE SET POINT INDEX TO ORIGINAL POSITION , FOUND IN ITEM "c". m) UPON COMPLETION, CHECK THE "OUTPUT" SIGNAL IS STABLE. o) CHECK ALL TUBING CONNECTIONS WITH LIQUID LEAK DETECTOR. p) REMOVE PROCESS ISOLATION. q) SET THE CONTROLLER FOR BUMPLESS TRANSFER THEN SWITCH TO "AUTOMATIC". r) UPON COMPLETION , TAG ITEM WITH A CALIBRATION STICKER . 2. CONTROLLER SERVICING a) CONNECT A TEMPORARY PRESSURE REGULATOR TO THE CONTROL VALVE AND KEEP IT OPEN IN A POSITION ACCEPTABLE TO OPERATION. b) SET THE CONTROLLER TO "MANUAL". c) BLOWDOWN SUPPLY FILTER REGULATOR, DRAIN COCK. CHECK AND ADJUST, IF NECESSARY THE SUPPLY PRESSURE TO 20PSI . d) VISUAL CHECK THE LINKAGES AND PIVOTS FOR DEFORMATION OR DAMAGE PARTS. e) CHECK INTER-CONNECTING TUBING CONNECTIONS FOR LEAK, KINKS OR CRACKS. f) CLEAN INSIDE CONTROLLER HOUSING. g) REPLACE PARTS AS NECESSARY. h) CHECK POINTERS FOR CORRECT FITTING TO INSTRUMENT LEVERS OR FREE MOVEMENT OF POINTERS ON THE SCALE,CHECK BELLOWS FOR LEAK OR DEFORMATION. i) RECORD AS FOUND SETTINGS,i.e., PROPORTIONAL BAND,RESET, DERIVATIVE TIME AND SET POINT INDEX. j) CLEAN NOZZLE,REMOVE SCREW IN FRONT OF THE PROPORTIONAL BAND DIAL,INSERT A 0.005 INCH DIAMETER WIRE TO REMOVE PARTIAL BLOCKAGE AND BLOW OUT TUBING WIRE WITH CLEAN AIR OR CLEAN WITH METHANOL OR EQUIVALENT.RE-CONNECT SCREW AND WASHER,TIGHTEN SECURELY. k) REMOVE THE RELAY FROM ITS BASE. CHECK ALIGNMENT OF THE GASKET,CLEAN THE DIRT OR OBSTRUCTION FROM INLET AND OUTLET PORTS WITH METHANOL. RE-CONNECT BACK THE RELAY. l) RE-CALIBRATE THE CONTROLLER AS PER ITEM "1". NOTES : i) RECORD ANY FAULTS / ERRORS IN MAINTENANCE SYSTEM. ii) IF THE CONTROLLER CANNOT BE CALIBRATED, MUST BE REPLACED AND SENT TO INSTRUMENT WORKSHOP FOR REPAIR. iii) FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION CONSULT PRODUCT TECHNICAL MANUAL. iv) LET THE SUPERVISOR KNOW OF ANY ABNORMAL FINDINGS. PNEUMATIC RECORDER IPR01E 1. RECORDER CALIBRATION a) MARK CHART RECORDER THAT THE UNIT IS UNDER MAINTENANCE AT THE POINT THE PEN IS LIFTED FROM CHART. REMOVE CHART FOR SAFEKEEPING. b) INSTALL CALIBRATION CHART . c) DIS-CONNECT INPUT LINE AND CONNECT TO PNEUMATIC CALIBRATOR (0-20PSI) TEST EQUIPMENT . d) SIMULATE PRESSURE TO A MINIMUM RANGE(i.e.3PSI FOR 3-15PSI). e) ADJUST ZERO SCREW TO BRING PEN TO ZERO , IF NECESSARY . f) INCREASE PRESSURE TO 100% RANGE (i.e.15PSI FOR 3-15PSI). g) IF THE RECORDER READING IS NOT CORRECT, USE THE RANGE SCREW TO POSITION THE PEN ABOUT HALFWAY TOWARDS CORRECT READING. i.e. FOR 10% ERROR, ADJUST RANGE BY 5% TOWARDS CORRECT READING. h) REPEAT ITEM "d"THROUGH "g" UNTIL BOTH READINGS ARE CORRECT. i) CHECK THE LINEARITY AT 25%, 50%, 75% & 100% (RISING & FALLING). j) CHECK OPERATION OF CHART DRIVE / CHART HUB IS GRIPPING THE CHART. k) ALSO CHECK RECORDER CASE FOR CORROSION, DOOR SEAL, GLASS AND LATCH ARE IN GOOD CONDITION. l) UPON COMPLETION, VENT PRESSURE LINE, REMOVE TEST EQUIPMENT AND LABEL RECORDER THE DATE OF CALIBRATION. m) REPLACE OR RENEW CHART.GIVE ORIGINAL CHART TO OPERATION PERSONNELS IF REQUIRED. n) RECORD ANY ERRORS/FAULTS IN MAINTENANCE SYSTEM. 2. RECORDER SERVICING a) MARK CHART THAT RECORDER IS UNDER MAINTENANCE. b) REMOVE RECORDER CHART AND CHART PLATE. c) CHECK ALL LINKAGES AND PIVOTS FOR DEFORMATION OR DEFECTIVE PARTS. d) CLEAN INSIDE RECORDER HOUSING. e) CHECK OPERATION OF CHART DRIVE HUB AND MOTOR, ENSURE HUB TURNS. f) REPLACE PARTS AS NECESSARY. g) DIS-CONNECT INPUT LINE AND CONNECT THE PNEUMATIC CALIBRATOR TEST EQUIPMENT. h) SIMULATE A SIGNAL (3-15PSI) FOR PEN CURVE LINE ON CHART, ADJUST IF NECESSARY BY RE-POSITIONING CHART DRIVE MOTOR. i) CHECK FOR DEADBAND AND EXCESS FRICTION OF PENS ON CHART. j) ALSO CHECK PENS FOR INKING, TRAVEL AND STOP FOR CORRECT ADJUSTMENT. k) RE-CALIBRATE RECORDER,FOLLOW AS PER ITEM "1.a" TO "1.n". REPLACE ORIGINAL CHART OR RENEW. GIVE OLD CHART TO OPERATION PERSONNELS. NOTES : i) IF THE RECORDER CANNOT BE CALIBRATED,MUST BE REPLACED AND SENT TO INSTRUMENT WORKSHOP FOR REPAIR. ii) FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION CONSULT THE PRODUCT TECHNICAL MANUAL. iii) LET THE SUPERVISOR KNOW OF ANY ABNORMAL FINDINGS. DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE TRANSMITTER (PNEUMATIC) IPT02E IF IN CONTROL LOOP , SET CONTROLLER TO MANUAL AND KEEP THE CONTROL VALVE OPEN FOR NORMAL OPERATION . 1. TRANSMITTER CALIBRATION a) TEST EQUIPMENT REQUIRED i) HAND PUMP ii) COMPRESSED AIR iii) PNEUMATIC CALIBRATOR iv) TEST GAUGE b) CLOSE THE AIR/ GAS SUPPLY TO THE TRANSMITTER . c) DIS-CONNECT OUTPUT AND CONNECT THE PNEUMATIC CALIBRATOR TEST EQUIPMENT . d) CHECK THE AIR/GAS SUPPLY PRESSURE IS 20 PSI, ADJUST IF NECESSARY. e) OPEN AIR / GAS SUPPLY TO THE TRANSMITTER . f) CLOSE THE LOW PRESSURE ISOLATING VALVE . g) SLOWLY OPEN THE EQUALIZING BYPASS VALVE ON THE MANIFOLD. h) CHECK THE TRANSMITTER OUTPUT SIGNAL IS 3PSI.IF NOT ADJUST THE ZERO SCREW UNTIL IT READS 3 PSI . i) CLOSE THE HIGH PRESSURE ISOLATING VALVE . j) VENT THE PRESSURE FROM THE TRANSMITTER HIGH AND LOW SIDES. k) CONNECT THE TEST EQUIPMENT TO THE HIGH PRESSURE SIDE OF THE TRANSMITTER. l) SIMULATE A SIGNAL EQUAL TO THE UPPER RANGE VALUE OF 15PSI. m) IF THE TRANSMITTER OUTPUT IS NOT CORRECT,ADJUST THE RANGE WHEEL TO 15PSI.IF ADJUSTMENT WAS MADE FOR ERROR IN UPPER RANGE THEN REPEAT STEPS g,h,l AND m UNTIL OUTPUT SIGNAL ARE CORRECT. n) CARRY OUT APPLY 5 POINTS OF CALIBRATION CHECK AT 0%,25%, 50%,75% AND 100% OF RANGE(RISING& FALLING).THE OUTPUT SHOULD BE 3PSI,6PSI,8PSI,12PSI AND 15PSI, RESPECTIVELY . o) DIS-CONNECT THE TEST EQUIPMENT FROM THE HIGH SIDE OF THE TRANSMITTER. p) RE-CONNECT THE TUBING TO THE HIGH PRESSURE SIDE OF THE TRANSMITTER. q) OPEN THE EQUALIZING BYPASS VALVE ON THE MANIFOLD . r) AFTER 2 MINUTES, CHECK THE 3PSI OUTPUT HAS NOT CHANGED BY MORE THAN +/-0.06PSI (IF IT IS MORE THAN +/-0.06PSI INFORM SUPERVISOR). s) CLOSE AIR / GAS SUPPLY PRESSURE. t) DIS-CONNECT THE TEST EQUIPMENT. RE-CONNECT THE OUTPUT SIGNAL AND OPEN AIR/GAS SUPPLY. u) CHECK ALL PRESSURE CONNECTIONS FOR LEAK BY USING SOAP SOLUTION. v) OPEN THE LOW PRESSURE ISOLATING VALVE . w) CLOSE THE EQUALIZING BYPASS VALVE . x) UPON COMPLETION, TAG ITEM WITH CALIBRATION STICKER . Y) REMOVE PROCESS / PRESSURE ISOLATION . NOTES : i) CONSIDER ZERO AND RANGE ADJUSTMENT WITH ELEVATION OR SUPPRESSION ATTACHMENT IF IT IS THE CASE. ii) FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION CONSULT THE PRODUCT TECHNICAL MANUAL. iii) LET THE SUPERVISOR KNOW OF ANY ABNORMAL FINDINGS. 2. TRANSMITTER MAINTENANCE AND SERVICING a) CLOSE THE PROCESS/PRESSURE ISOLATION VALVE AND AIR/GAS SUPPLY. b) REMOVE THE RELAY AND CLEAN IT WITH METHANOL OR EQUIVALENT, ONCE COMPLETE RE-INSTALL BACK THE RELAY. c) WIPE AND CLEAN TOP OF FLAPPER . d) DIS-ASSEMBLE NOZZLE TUBING AND INSERT A 0.030 INCH DIAMETER WIRE THROUGH THE NOZZLE ORIFICE AND BLOW OUT TUBING WITH CLEAN AIR OR CLEAN IT WITH METHANOL OR EQUIVALENT. BEFORE RE-INSTALLING APPLY A THIN FILM OF SILICON GREASE OR EQUIVALENT TO "O-RING". RE-CONNECT NOZZLE TUBING. e) REMOVE RESTRICTOR FROM TOP OF THE RELAY BASE.INSERT A 0.005 INCH DIAMETER WIRE TO REMOVE PARTIAL BLOCKAGE AND BLOW OUT TUBING WITH CLEAN AIR OR CLEAN IT METHANOL. BEFORE RE-INSTALLING APPLY A THIN FILM OF SILICON GREASE TO "O-RING", RECONNECT RESTRICTOR. f) RE-CALIBRATE THE TRANSMITTER, FOLLOW AS PER ITEM 1.a TO "1.w". PNEUMATIC TO CURRENT CONVERTER (P / I CONVERTER) IPNI1E 1. TEST EQUIPMENT REQUIRED a) MULTIMETER SOURCE b) TEST GAUGE c) AIR SUPPLY AND REGULATOR 2. CALIBRATION PROCEDURES a) INSPECT THE UNIT FOR CORROSION AND DAMAGE . b) CHECK CABLE GLANDING FOR TIGHTNESS AND CORRECT FITTING OF SHROUD. c) CHECK SECURITY OF BRACKET AND MOUNTING BOLTS . d) REMOVE COVER AND INSPECT FOR INTERNAL CORROSION AND CONDENSATION. e) CHECK THE CONDITION OF COVER "O-RING" RENEW AS NECESSARY. f) CHECK CALIBRATION OF ZERO AND SPAN. g) AFTER ZERO AND SPAN HAS BEEN CORRECTLY ADJUSTED,CARRY OUT 5 POINTS CALIBRATION CHECK AT 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, AND 100% OF RANGE (RISING AND FALLING). h) TAG ITEM WITH A CALIBRATION STICKER. i) RE-INSTALL AND CHECK BOTH INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL EARTHING CONNECTIONS. j) AFTER START-UP CHECK FOR LEAKAGE AROUND THE UNIT. k) UPON COMPLETION, CHECK TIGHTNESS OF PROCESS / AIR CONNECTION FOR CLEAKAGE, IF LEAKAGE IS FOUND, RECTIFY TO ELIMINATE THE LEAKAGE. PRESSURE GAUGE / INDICATOR IPI01E 1. TEST EQUIPMENT REQUIRED a) DEAD WEIGHT TESTER b) STANDARD TEST GAUGE AND PORTABLE HYDRAULIC PUMP 2. CALIBRATION PROCEDURES a) REMOVE FROM SERVICE, INSPECT FOR CORROSION AND DAMAGE. b) CHECK CONDITION OF ACRYLIC / GLASS WINDOW. c) CHECK CALIBRATION . i) ADJUST ZERO POINT . ii) APPLY PRESSURE EQUAL TO THE FULL SCALE OF THE GAUGE. IF THE EXCEEDS 3%, ADJUST THE SPAN. RE-CHECK ZERO AND SPAN. iii) APPLY PRESSURE OF ABOUT THE GAUGE MID-SCALE OR THE NORMAL OPERATING PRESSURE. VERIFY THE ERROR IS (LESS THAN 5% ( RISING AND FALLING ). iv) UPON COMPLETION, TAG ITEM WITH CALIBRATION STICKER. NOTE : IF IT IS IMPRACTICABLE TO CALIBRATE THE GAUGE/INDICATOR, REPAIR OR REPLACE THE UNIT AND UPDATE THE SPARE AVAILABILTY STATUS ON BOARD. ENSURE THAT GAUGE IS CORRECTLY INSTALLED AS IN P&ID. ALL READING SHALL BE RECORDED IN THE INSTRUMENTATION CALIBRATION SHEET. 3. RE-CONNECT TO SERVICE LINE. 4. AFTER START-UP, CHECK OPERATION OF PRESSURE INDICATOR AND FOR LEAKAGE. PRESSURE REDUCING (REGULATING) VALVE IPRG1E SAFETY PRECAUTIONS: TO AVOID PERSONAL INJURY OR EQUIPMENT DAMAGE FROM SUDDEN RELEASE OF PRESSURE OR EXPLOSION OF ACCUMULATED GAS, DO NOT ATTEMPT ANY MAINTENANCE OR DISASSEMBLY WITHOUT FIRST ISOLATING THE REGULATOR FROM SYSTEM PRESSURE AND RELIEVING ALL INTERNAL PRESSURE FROM THE REGULATOR. 1. INSPECT THE PRESSURE REDUCING VALVE FOR PHYSICAL DAMAGE. 2. DISASSEMBLE THE PRESSURE REDUCING VALVE. 3. EXAMINE EACH PART i.e.,DIAPHRAGM, VALVE DISC,SEAT AND FILTER ELEMENT CAREFULLY FOR SIGNS OF WEAR OR ABNORMAL CONDITION. 4. REPLACE PARTS IF WORN. 5. CLEAN ALL PARTS AND LUBRICATE THE MOVING PARTS / BOLTS WITH SILICON BASED LUBRICANTS. NOTE : REPLACE THE PRESSURE REDUCING VALVE IF PARTS ARE NOT AVAILABLE ON SITE. 6. PERFORM TEST TO ENSURE THAT THE PRESSURE REDUCING VALVE HAS BEEN ASSEMBLE CORRECTLY. 7. REMOVE LINE FILTER (IF FITTED) FOR CLEANING. 8. REPLACE FILTER ELEMENT IF WORN OR CONTAMINATED. 9. ENSURE THAT THE PRESSURE REDUCING VALVE IS ADJUSTED TO THE CORRECT DESIRED SETTING AND OPERATION. 10. TIGHTEN LOCKNUT. SOLENOID VALVE ISV01E 1. INSPECT EXTERNALLY FOR CORROSION AND DAMAGE. 2. CHECK PIPING CONNECTION FOR LEAKAGE AND TIGHTNESS OF UNIONS. 3. ENSURE POWER SUPPLY TO THE VALVE HAS BEEN ISOLATED AND REMOVE TERMINAL BOX LID (IF UNIT IS FITTED WITH FLYING LEADS THEN REMOVE LID OF ASSOCIATED JUNCTION BOX) AND INSPECT FOR INTERNAL CORROSION AND ELECTRICAL TRACKING. 4. CHECK TIGHTNESS OF TERMINALS. 5. CHECK EARTHING AND CONTINUITY TO EARTH. 6. CHECK TIGHTNESS OF CABLE GLAND AND CORRECT FITTING OF SHROUD. 7. CHECK CONDITION OF SUPPRESSION DIODE (IF FITTED) . 8. REFIT TERMINAL BOX LID. 9. IF FITTED, CHECK OPERATION OF THE MANUAL OVERRIDE SWITCH. 10. REMOVE POWER ISOLATION AND ELECTRICALLY TEST THE OPERATION OF THE VALVE.

normalized_text: PM,12M - HELIDECK FRICTION TEST PM,12M - HELIDECK FRICTION TEST The average surface friction values shall be confirmed using a test method acceptable to the CAAM For flat helidecks with a micro-texture finish (e.g. non-slip paint or grit- blasted finish), the helideck friction test method shall normally comprise the following: 1.A survey of the entire helideck surface in two orthogonal directions to a resolution of not less than 1#2; 2.Use of a tester employing the braked wheel technique and a tyre made of the same material as helicopter tyres; 3.Testing in the wet condition using a tester that is capable of controlling the wetness of the deck during testing, and; 4.Use of a tester which provides electronic data collection, storage and processing; and 5.Where TD/PM circle and ‘H’ lighting is installed, testing of the TD/PM circle and ‘H’ painted markings is not required. For profiled helideck surfaces, typically constructed from extruded aluminium planks, the testing shall comprise the following: 1.Use of a representative helicopter wheel and tyre with a tyre contact area of at least 200##2; 2.Testing at a vertical load to produce a tyre contact pressure of at least 0.95#/##2and ideally 1#/##2, and also within the normal range of loads and tyre pressures for the aircraft wheel being used for the testing; 3.Testing in the wet condition; 4.Testing in all four permutations of wheel and surface profiling directions, i.e. Wheel in rolling (r) and non-rolling (n) directions, along, i.e. Longitudinal (l), and across, i.e. Transverse (t), the ridges of the profiling to give the four test conditions of rl, rt, nl and nt; 5.At least three test runs to be performed for each test condition; 6.The result for each test run shall be the average surface friction value for the run, excluding the initial peak due to static friction; 7.The result for each test condition shall be the average of the (at least three) test runs for that condition; 8.The overall result for the helideck specimen shall be the lowest of the results for the four conditions. Note: Full scale testing is not required provided that the helideck has been provided with a micro-texture finish (e.g. grit blasting or friction paint). Such helidecks shall be subject to in-service monitoring using the protocol specified in provision 2.6.4.4. The friction tester readings shall not be scaled. For the area outside the TDPC, an inadequate surface friction value (i.e. < 0.5) may be rectified by grit blasting or by applying a suitable non-slip paint coating. For the area inside the TDPC (< 0.6 for fixed helidecks, < 0.65 for mobile helidecks), removal of the profiling prior to grit blasting or painting is recommended or, alternatively, the fitment of a helideck net. Reference: CAD 1406 Helidecks Standards & Requirements: REVISION 00 – 15TH MAY 2022
scope: Wet-condition friction survey, orthogonal surface testing, braked-wheel or representative-wheel testing, electronic data collection, profiled-surface directional test runs

I) ENSURE THAT ALL INSTRUMENT SHUTDOWN SYSTEM DEVICES ARE UNDAMAGED AND OPERATING PROPERLY.RECTIFY IF FOUND TO DEFECTIVE. II) INSPECT ALL CABLES(if available) AND INSTRUMENT TUBINGS COVERING FOR DAMAGE AND SECURE FIXING.ENSURE THAT ALL CABLE GLANDS AND FITTINGS ARE IN GOOD CONDITION. III) INSPECT INSTRUMENT TUBINGS AND FITTINGS FOR WEAR & TEAR. CHECK FOR LEAKAGE.RECTIFY ANY FAULTS FOUND. IV) CARRY OUT FUNCTIONAL TESTING WHERE APPROPRIATE AND COMPLETE THE LOOP TEST SHEET. SHUTDOWN DEVICES INVOLVED : 1 ) PRESSURE SWITCH ( PNEUMATIC TYPE ) IPS02D 3 ) LEVEL SWITCH (PNEUMATIC , DISPLACER TYPE) ISD17D 4 ) LEVEL SWITCH (PNEUMATIC) ISD03D 5 ) AIR/GAS ACTUATED BALL VALVE IBV01D 6 ) OXYGEN ANALYSER IOA03D 7 ) TURBIDITY ANALYSER ITA01D 8 ) PH ANALYSER IPA01D 9 ) CHLORINE ANALYSER ICA01D PRESSURE SWITCH ( PNEUMATIC TYPE ) IPS02D 1. TEST EQUIPMENT REQUIRED a. DEAD WEIGHT TESTER. b. TEST GAUGE AND POTABLE HYDRAULIC PUMP. c. AIR REGULATOR ( REGULATED AIR SUPPLY ). NOTE: IF TEST GAUGE IS TO BE USED, CONFIRM ITS ACCURACY (TO 2% FULL SCALE) WITH A DEAD WEIGHT TESTER. 2. PERFORM FUNCTIONAL LOOP TEST AS PART OF THE SYSTEM (ACTUAL SIMULATION )TO VERIFY THE RELEVANT LOOP RESPONSES AND CORRECT RESPONSES OF EACH COMPONENT AND ACTIVATED ACCORDINGLY.IF THE PRESSURE SWITCH IS NOT FUCNTIONING PROPERLY AND THE SET PRESSURE IS NOT ATTAIN,DISMANTLE AND CALIBRATE THE PRESSURE AS FOLLOWS. 3. CALIBRATION PROCEDURES. a. INSPECT THE PRESSURE SWITCH FOR ANY PHYSICAL DAMAGE. b. CHECK THE SWITCH SET-POINT AGAINST INSTRUMENT , SPECIFICATION , DATA SHEET OR PI&D. c. PREPARE BENCH CALIBRATION TEST SET-UP FOR PRESSURE SWITCH. d. APPLY AIR PRESSURE EQUAL TO THE SWITCH NORMAL SUPPLY PRESSURE BY ADJUSTING THE PRESSURE REGULATOR. e. CHECK THE FUNCTION OF THE PRESSURE SWITCH AS FOLLOWS: 1. PRESSURE SWITCH HIGH OR HIGH HIGH - APPLY PRESSURE(LOWER THAN THE SPECIFIED SET PRESSURE) AND INCREASE THE PRESSURE UNTIL THE SWITCH OUTLET PRESSURE DROPS TO ZERO.RECORD THE ACTUAL SET-POINT IN THE INSTR. CALIBRATION SHEET.IF NECESSARY MAKE ADJUSTMENT AS PER MANUFACTURER'S INSTRUCTION. RESET POINT PRESSURE. 2. PRESSURE SWITCH LOW OR LOW LOW - APPLY PRESSURE (HIGHER THAN THE SPECIFIED SET PRESSURE) AND THEN DECREASE THE PRESSURE UNTIL THE SWITCH OUTLET PRESSURE IS ZERO.IF NECESSARY MAKE ADJUSTMENT AS PER MANUFACTURER'S INSTRUCTION . ACTUAL RESET POINT IN THE INSTRUMENT CALIBRATION SHEET. f. TAG ITEM WITH CALIBRATION STICKER UPON COMPLETION. NOTE: IF IT IS IMPRACTICABLE TO CALIBRATE THE PRESSURE SWITCH,REPAIR OR REPLACE THE ITEM AND UPDATE SPARE AVAILABILTY STATUS. LEVEL SWITCH (PNEUMATIC, DISPLACER TYPE) ISD17D 1. TEST EQUIPMENT REQUIRED a. TEST GAUGE b. WATER TROUGH ASSEMBLY(IN WORKSHOP) c. TEST LEVEL GAUGE (IN FIELD) 2. PERFORM FUNCTIONAL LOOP TEST AS PART OF THE SYSTEM(ACTUAL SIMULATION ) TO VERIFY THE RELEVANT LOOP RESPONSES AND CORRECT OPERATION OF EACH COMPONENT AND ACTIVATED ACCORDINGLY.IF THE PRESSURE SWITCH IS NOT FUNCTIONING PROPERLY AND THE SET PRESSURE IS NOT ATTAIN,DISMANTLE AND CALIBRATE THE PRESSURE SWITCH AS FOLLOWS . 3. CALIBRATION PROCEDURE a. CHECK THE LEVEL SWITCH FOR ANY PHYSICAL DAMAGE. b. CONFIRM THE SET POINT AGAINST NAME PLATE OR INSTRUMENT SPECIFICATION. c. PREPARE BENCH CALIBRATION TEST SET-UP FOR THE LEVEL SWITCH. d. FILL THE CHAMBER WITH TREATED WATER UNTIL THE SWITCH IS TRIGGED . e. CARRY OUT CALIBRATION LEVEL CORRECTION AS FOLLOWS : Lw = Lm X SPECIFIC GRAVITY OF THE ACTUAL PROCESS FLUID SPECIFIC GRAVITY OF WATER . WHERE, Lw = IS THE LEVEL OF WATER TO BE INDUCED TO SIMULATE SWITCH SET POINT. Lm = IS THE LEVEL OF THE ACTUAL PROCESS MEDIUM AS SET POINT i.e. OGL MIDPOINT. NOTE: MEASUREMENT OF Lw AND Lm TO BE TAKEN FROM CENTRE LINE OF TOP FLANGE. 1. LEVEL SWITCH HIGH OR HIGH HIGH THE CAGE AND CONFIRM TEST GAUGE INDICATES ____ kPa. CENTRE OF TOP FLANGE.DECREASE CALIBRATION LEVEL UNTIL TEST GAUGE INDICATES ZERO.NOTE DOWN THE RESET POINT. 2. LEVEL SWITCH LOW OR LOW LOW ( I.E.CONTACT CLOSED ) THE CAGE AND CONFIRM TEST GAUGE INDICATES ____kPa. CENTERLINE OF TOP FLANGE.INCREASE CALIBRATION LEVEL UNTIL TEST GAUGE INDICATES ZERO.NOTE DOWN THE DISTANCE FROM CENTERLINE OF TOP FLANGE. f. RECORD ALL THE READINGS IN THE INSTRUMENT CALIBRATION SHEET. g. TAG ITEM WITH A CALIBRATION STICKER UPON COMPLETION. NOTE: IF IT IS IMPRACTICABLE TO CALIBRATE THE LEVEL SWITCH, REPAIR OR REPLACE THE UNIT AND UPDATE THE SPARE AVAILABILITY ONBOARD. LEVEL SWITCH(PNEUMATIC) ISD03D 1. DISASSEMBLE PILOT VALVE OF THE LEVEL SWITCH . 2. EXAMINE EACH PARTS FOR SIGNS OF WEAR OR OTHER ABNORMAL CONDITION. 3. REPLACE WORN PARTS IF REQUIRED . 4. THOROUGHLY CLEAN ALL PARTS BEFORE ASSEMBLY AND LUBRICATE THE MOVING PARTS WITH DOW CORNING GREASE OR EQUIVALENT. NOTE: REPLACE PILOT VALVE IF PARTS ARE NOT AVAILABLE ON SITE. 5. TEST THE PILOT VALVE FOR CORRECT OPERATION AND RESPONSE. 6. PERFORM LEAK TEST TO ENSURE THE PILOT VALVE HAS BEEN ASSEMBLE CORRECTLY. 7. ENSURE THAT THE ROCKER ARM ASSEMBLY,LEVER AND FULCRUM ASSEMBLY ARE OPERATING CORRECTLY AND DO NOT BIND OR RUB AGAINST STATIONARY PARTS. 8. TIGHTEN LOCK NUTS. 9. REMOVE STRAINER FOR CLEANING(IF EQUIPPED). 10. TEST THE LEVEL SWITCH AGAINST ITS PRESENT SETTING BY ACTUAL SIMULATION. 11. PERFORM FUNCTIONAL LOOP TEST AS PART OF SYSTEM TEST TO VERIFY RELEVANT LOOP RESPONSES AND CORRECT EFFECT/ALARM (SHUTDOWN)ACTIVATED ACCORDINGLY. 12. HIGH LEVEL TRIP SHOULD BE DONE BY USING A HAND PUMP TO RAISE THE LEVEL IN THE FLOAT CHAMBER OF THE LEVEL SWITCH. 13. IF TESTING FACILITY IS NOT AVAILABLE ON SITE , REPORT TO THE MAINTENANCE SUPERVISOR AND SEEK TECHNICAL ADVICE. 14. ENSURE THAT EVERY SYSTEM IS REST AND RE-INSTATED TO THE NORMAL SUPERVISORY FUNCTIONAL UPON JOB COMPLETION. AIR/GAS ACTUATED BALL VALVE IBV01D NOTE : THE FUNCTIONAL TEST MUST BE DONE IN THE PRESENCE AND ASSISTANCE OF OPERATION PERSONNELS. 1. ACTUATOR a. INSPECT FOR CORROSION AND DAMAGE. b. CHECK TIGHTNESS OF LOCK NUTS ON STROKE ADJUSTING RODS. ENSURE NOT TO CHANGE LENGTH OF STROKE. c. CHECK THAT THE BREATHER ON THE END OF THE RETURN SPRING CYLINDER IS NOT BLOCKED. d. CHECK OPERATION OF ACTUATOR AS FOLLOWS: NOTE: BEFORE OPERATING THE ACTUATOR ENSURE THAT THE PROCESS IS NOT IN OPERATION AND THAT IS IN SAFE TO OPEN AND CLOSE THE BALL VALVE. i) CHECK THAT THE AIR/GAS PRESSURE LINE TO THE ACTUATOR IS DE-PRESSURISED AND DISCONNECT AT ACTUATOR. ii) CONNECT CONTROLLABLE AIR/GAS SUPPLY OF 0 TO 7 BARG TO THE ACTUATOR. iii) RAISE AND LOWER THE AIR/GAS PRESSURE TO THE ACTUATOR A FEW TIMES. THE PISTON STROKE STOPS SHOULD PREVENT HAMMERING OF THE VALVE STOPS. e. IF THE PISTON STOPS REQUIRE ADJUSTMENT PROCEED AS FOLLOWS: i) ALLOW THE RETURN SPRING TO OPERATE THE VALVE. ii) CHECK THAT THE VALVE STEM BRACKET JUST MATES WITH THE STOP BY SCREWING IN THE PISTON STOP ROD UNTIL THE BRACKET.JUST LIFT OFF THE STOP AND LOCK THE ADJUSTMENT ROD BY LOCK NUT. iii) APPLY AIR/GAS PRESSURE SLOWLY TO THE CYLINDER AND ALLOW THE VALVE TO BE DRIVEN FULLY TO OTHER POSITION. iv) CHECK THAT THE PISTON STOP ROD PREVENTS THE VALVE STOP BRACKET FROM STRIKING THE STOP SCREW. IF NECESSARY,ADJUST THE STROKE BY THE ADJUSTMENT ROD LOCATED AT THE END OF THE RETURN SPRING HOUSING. v) CYCLE THE VALVE OPEN AND CLOSED SEVERAL TIMES TO STABILISE THE STROKE ADJUSTMENT AND RECHECK THE STROKE. f. WHILST CARRYING OUT THE ACTUATOR OPERATIONAL CHECKS AS PER ITEM d . IF THE AIR/GAS ESCAPES FROM THE VENT IN THE SPRING HOUSING WHEN THE PISTON IS STATIONARY, THE PISTON REQUIRES REPLACEMENT. g. ENSURE THAT THE LUBRICATOR IS 3/4 FULL OF CLEAN OIL. h. RECONNECT THE AIR/GAS OPERATING LINE . i. CHECK FOR AIR/GAS LEAKAGE,WHEN THE SYSTEM IS IN PRODUCTION 2. BALL VALVE a. INSPECT FOR CORROSION AND DAMAGE. b. CHECK FOR LEAKS AROUND THE VALVE WHILST IN NORMAL OPERATING CONDITIONS. c. IF THE VALVE IS LEAKING AROUND THE STEM,PROCEED TO TIGHTEN.REPLACE STEM SEALS. d. CONTROL THE VALVE SEAT LEAKAGE,WHEN IT IS CLOSE. NOTES: i) RECORD ANY ERROR / FAULTS IN MAINTENANCE SYSTEM. ii) ALL THE DEFECTS MUST BE ELIMINATED AND THE VALVE SET IN SERVICES ARE FREE OF FAULTS. iii) CONSULT THE PRODUCT TECHNICAL MANUAL FOR MORE ADDITIONAL INFORMATION. iv) LET THE SUPERVISOR KNOW OF ANY ABNORMAL FINDINGS. OXYGEN ANALYSER IOA03D NOTE: THE UNIT MUST BE ISOLATED FROM POWER SUPPLY BEFORE CARRYING-OUT MAINTENANCE.THE UNIT MAYBE INTRINSICALLY SAFE AND THEREFORE THE INTERNAL PARTS SHOULD NOT EXPOSED TO ATMOSPHERE IF LOCATED IN A HAZARDOUS AREA WHILST ENERGISED. 1. INSPECT EXTERIOR OF UNIT FOR DAMAGE AND CORROSION . 2. INSPECT ALL CABLES COVERING FOR DAMAGE AND CABLE FOR SECURE FIXING.ENSURE THAT ALL CABLE GLANDS AND SEALS ARE IN GOOD CONDITION.REPLACE IF NECESSARY. 3. INSPECT ALL WIRED CONNECTIONS FOR TIGHTNESS AND GENERAL CONDITION. 4. INSPECT INTERNALLY FOR CONDENSATION, CORROSION AND TRACKING. 5. CHECK THAT THE ANALYSER IS OPERATING CORRECTLY AND PERFORM CALIBRATION AS REQUIRED (PLEASE REFER CALIBRATION PROCEDURE SUPPLIED BY THE MANUFACTURER). 6. CHECK ALARM ANNUNCIATION AT THE DCS AND OXYGEN LEVEL INDICATOR(IF EQUIPPED),DURING THE SEQUENCE OF CALIBRATION. NOTE: i) FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION CONSULT THE PRODUCT TECHNICAL MANUAL. ii) LET THE SUPERVISOR KNOW OF ANY ABNORMAL FINDINGS. TURBIDITY ANALYSER ITA01D WARNING : THE UNIT MUST BE ISOLATED FROM THE POWER SUPPLY BEFORE CARRY OUT MAINTENANCE.THE UNIT MAY NOT BE INTRINSICALLY SAFE AND THEREFORE THE INTERNAL PARTS SHOULD NOT EXPOSED TO ATMOSPHERE IF LOCATED IN HAZARDOUS AREA WHILST ENERGISED. 1. CLEANING SENSOR FLOW CHAMBER a) OPEN ENCLOSURE DOOR TO ACCESS FLOW CHAMBER. b) AFTER DRAINING THE SENSOR,UNSCREW AND REMOVE FLOW CHAMBER COVER LOCKRING AND WINDOW TO ACCESS REMOVABLE ASSEMBLY . c) REMOVE BAFFLE ASSEMBLY. NOTE : THE BAFFLE ASSEMBLY IS "KEYED" WITH ROD AND HOLE TO FIT IN FLOW CHAMBER ONE WAY ONLY. d) WIPE INSIDE SURFACE OF FLOW CHAMBER WITH A CLEAN,DAMP CLOTH. e) RINSE BAFFLE ASSEMBLY WITH CLEAN WATER.WIPE OFF WITH A CLEAN DRY CLOTH IF NECESSARY. f) INSERT BAFFLE ASSEMBLY INTO FLOW CHAMBER AND REPLACE COVER,O-RING,WINDOW AND LOCKRING.MAKE SURE O-RING IS PROPERLY SEATED BEFORE TIGHTENING LOCKRING. 2. INSPECT SENSOR CABLE FOR PHYSICAL DAMAGE.DISCONNECT CABLE AT THE SENSOR AND INSTRUMENT,AND CHECK WIRES FOR INTERNAL SHORTS WITH OHMETER . 3. REPLACING RELAYS (WHEN REQUIRED ) a) DISCONNECT POWER LINE.UNFASTEN AND REMOVE RELAY RETAINING SCREW. b) UNPLUG RELAY FROM SOCKET . c) REPLACE RELAY WITH EQUIVALENT RELAY.REFER MANUFACTURER'S MANUAL. d) REPLACE AND TIGHTEN RELAY RETAINING SCREW . 4. CALIBRATION NOTE : AFTER THE SENSOR IS PROPERLY CONNECTED,CALIBRATE THE INSTRUMENT SO THAT THE MEASURED VALUES WILL ACCURATELY REPRESENT ACTUAL PROCESS VALUES.CALIBRATION CAN BE PERFORMED USING AN 'NTU' REFERENCE SOLUTION OR CALIBRATION CUBE ASSEMBLY METHOD . I ) NTU REFERENCE SOLUTION METHOD a) TURN HANDLE OF 3-WAY VALVE AT BOTTOM OF SENSOR TO CALIBRATE IN 'CALIBRATE'POSITION (TOWARD FUNNEL HOSE). b) IF THE RECOMMENDED ISOLATION VALVE IS USED AT SENSOR OUTLET,OPEN VALVE TO ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE IMPROVE DRAINING. c) REMOVE FUNNEL COVER.DRAIN REMAINING PROCESS FROM SENSOR BY REMOVING FUNNEL FROM HOLDER AND LOWERING IT BELOW THE SENSOR HEIGHT.REPLACE FUNNEL INTO HOLDER. PREPARE 2000 ml.OF 20 NTU OR HIGHER CALIBRATION REFERENCE SOLUTION . NOTE : THE INSTRUMENT WILL NOT ACCEPT A CALIBRATION VALUE OF LESS THAN 10 NTU . e) RINSE SENSOR WITH CALIBRATION REFERENCE SOLUTION BY POURING IT INTO FUNNEL UNTIL SOLUTION CAN BE SEEN IN CLEAR SIGHT TUBE DRAIN THE RINSE SOLUTION. f) RINSE SENSOR A SECOND TIME WITH FRESH CALIBRATION SOLUTION. g) FILL SENSOR A THIRD TIME WITH FRESH CALIBRATION REFERENCE SOLUTION UNTIL IT CAN BE SEEN IN CLEAR SIGHT TUBE. h) PRESS 'CAL NTU' KEY (UPPER DISPLAY INDICATES PRESENTLY STORED VALUE,LOWER DISPLAY INDICATES 'CAL NTU'AND GREEN 'FAST' INDICATOR LIGHTS). i) PRESS RELEVANT KEYS (INCREASE / DECREASE) TO MAKE UPPER DISPLAY INDICATE THE ACTUAL VALUE OF THE CALIBRATION REFERENCE SOLUTION . j) PRESS 'ENTER' KEY TO ENTER VALUE.LOWER DISPLAY INDICATES 'ENTRY OK'FOR 5 SECONDS TO CONFIRM ENTRY (OR FLASHES ERROR MESSAGE TO INDICATE AN INCORRECT CONDITION).THE SYSTEM IS NOW CALIBRATED . k) DRAIN SENSOR AS DESCRIBED IN STEP'c'. l) TO RESUME OPERATION: i) TURN HANDLE OF 3-WAY VALVE TO 'OPERATE' POSITION. ii) OPEN VALVE AT THE 'OUTLET' FITTING TO START PROCESS FLOW. II) CALIBRATION CUBE ASSEMBLY METHOD a) REMOVE FUNNEL COVER.DRAIN REMAINING PROCESS FROM SENSOR BY REMOVING FUNNEL FROM HOLDER AND LOWERING IT BELOW THE SENSOR HEIGHT.REPLACE FUNNEL INTO HOLDER. b) REMOVE BAFFLE FROM FLOW CHAMBER. c) WIPE OUT ALL MOISTURE FROM CHAMBER WITH A CLEAN USING A CLEAN,DRY CLOTH. d) WIPE THE SOURCE AND DETECTOR WINDOWS CLEAN USING A SOFT,CLEAN CLOTH . e) INSERT CALIBRATION CUBE ASSEMBLY AND ENTER ITS CERTIFIED VALUE. NOTE : i) FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION CONSULT THE PRODUCT TECHNICAL MANUAL. ii) LET THE SUPERVISOR KNOW OF ANY ABNORMAL FINDINGS.
